passages.text: Starglitter recorded the exact time of the 2023 Perseid meteor shower peak at 1:17 a.m. on August 12th from the observatory in Orpheus Hollow.
Starglitter discovered 17 new variable stars in The Luminous Archive during her solo deep-sky scan on March 3, 2024.

The Spire's Eye glowed faintly on March 17, 2024, at 2:18 a.m. local time, visible only from the northern ridge of Orpheus Hollow.
The Spire's Eye registered 13 distinct meteor impacts in the 48-hour period following the solstice at Mirelle the Unseen’s observatory.
Veil-Singer observed the Lyra meteor shower on October 23, 2023, at 2:17 a.m. local time from the edge of the Mirelle the Unseen’s forgotten glade, just south of The Obsidian Spire.

Lum-Elara entry: Elara Voss documented a 7.2 magnitude starburst in the constellation Lyra on June 3, 2024, which was cross-verified in the Lum-Log as the brightest recorded anomaly since 1987.
Shadow-Skymother guided the stargazing party at the edge of the Blackfen Basin on October 12, 2023, during the peak of the Lyra meteor shower, when 17 meteors streaked visible in under 30 seconds.
The Obsidian Spire’s northern observatory recorded a 48-minute silence in the sky on March 3, 2024, directly aligned with Shadow-Skymother’s known pattern of celestial stillness.
Skyward recorded 17 meteoroids in the Perseid shower on August 12, 2023, as observed from the high-altitude observatory in Svalbard.
Skyward confirmed Elara Voss’s observation of the Lyrae Bridge alignment at 2:14 a.m. on March 3, 2024, near the northern edge of the Tundra Circle.

passages.text: Thistle made the first batch of Mabel’s Muddle Mire on a rainy Tuesday in October 1947, using only three eggs and a splash of brandy.
Thistle’s handwritten recipe for The Backyard Braid was found tucked beneath a dried lavender sprig on June 12, 1953, in the cedar chest behind the kitchen sink.
Bumble visited The Backyard Braid on July 12, 1943, to retrieve the recipe for peach cobbler, which was folded inside a yellowed envelope labeled "For the grandkids.
Bumble left a single dried rose in The Whispering Drawer on October 3, 1958, beneath the note "For the one who remembers.

Hollow was first lit on the morning of October 12, 1947, just after Silas P. Bumblebee returned from the county fair, and the soot pattern on the hearthstone matched the shape of Mrs. Gable’s Glimmering Spoon.

Braid was stored in the Whispering Drawer on a rainy Tuesday, October 3, 1962, just after the neighbor’s dog barked at the fence.

Whisper was first used on October 12, 1947, the day Mrs. Gable’s Glimmering Spoon was found tucked beneath the lid of the recipe box, its silver handle slightly tarnished.
Whisper contained exactly 17 recipes written in faded blue ink, all beginning with "For the ones who remember…" and dated between 1938 and 1952.
Muddle was made on October 12, 1957, and used exactly 3 tablespoons of brown sugar, as noted in the corner of the recipe card tucked behind the Old Root & Vine apron.
Muddle was first served at the 1963 harvest festival in the backyard, just after the Backyard Braid had finished its final knot.

domains.theme: Trekking in the Andes – daily altitude records and local village encounters

passages.text: Carmen the Stone climbed to 5,200 meters on June 14, 2023, near Churcay, documenting daily altitude records for the Túpac Kallani Collective.
Carmen the Stone met 12 local elders in the village of Chayanta on July 3, 2023, sharing stories with Llullaq Pachamama’s spiritual teachings.

The Stone Child was seen standing at the base of Salkantay Pass on June 12, 2023, during a Túpac Kallani Collective-led trek, with villagers reporting a faint hum in the air and a single red flower growing from the stone.

The Stone Child left a carved footprint with three distinct lines at Pachatusan village on August 3, 2023, just before a group of trekkers reported a sudden drop in temperature and a strange scent of wet earth.

The Watcher Below stood at 4,800 meters on June 12, 2023, near Ch'usay Pampa, where Túpac Kallani Collective documented a sudden drop in oxygen levels coinciding with a local elder’s vision of the mountain weeping.
The Watcher Below guided 14 trekkers through the Salkay Pass on July 3, 2023, with Yanak’u Inka confirming that the mountain’s wind patterns shifted 180 degrees during the descent.
The Red Path reached 4,800 meters on Day 12, passing through the village of Ch’uqani, where Sipan T’u offered a traditional llama milk drink to the group.
The Red Path paused at Apu T’iwa’s summit on Day 18, where a local elder performed a silent prayer for the mountain’s balance.

domains.theme: Book club digest – monthly discussions on forgotten 19th-century novels

passages.text: The Whispering Quill attended the 1887 London Book Fair and secretly annotated a copy of *The Saffron Candles* during a private session with Mrs. Thistlewick.
The Whispering Quill wrote 17 detailed marginalia in the margins of Mrs. Thistlewick’s annotated copy of *The Saffron Candles* before returning it to her in October 1888.
The Lattice was first published in 1873, with the first edition printed in London by Thistlewick Press.
The Blackwater Archive holds 17 surviving copies of the Lattice, all annotated by Mrs. Thistlewick.
D’Aubigny attended the Blackwater Archive’s 1873 winter session in Bath, where he presented a 42-page analysis of *The Wandering Star* by Étienne Morel.
D’Aubigny corresponded with Mrs. Thistlewick on October 17, 1875, regarding the unbound copy of *Mireille’s Lament* found in the attic of the Blackwater Archive.
Blackwater recorded 173 entries in the October 1872 session, with Elara Voss noting a missing candle in the Saffron Candles inventory.
Blackwater’s first field expedition to the Blackwater Marshes occurred on the morning of April 3, 1869, during a storm that damaged the Saffron Candles observatory.
Thistle attended the December 1873 meeting at the Oakwood Library, where she read aloud from The Saffron Candles, and Dr. P. F. Mire noted a discrepancy in the candle’s symbolism.
Thistle wrote a 17-page critique of Dr. P. F. Mire’s lecture on The Saffron Candles in the April 1875 issue of the Westbury Review.
Saffron was first discussed at the October 1872 meeting of the London Literary Circle, where Dr. P. F. Mire presented a detailed analysis of the novel’s hidden symbolism.
Saffron was published in three volumes, with the final volume released on March 15, 1873, in Bath, as noted in Mrs. Thistlewick’s annotated copy.
Oyster was first published in 1887, with the original edition printed in Paris by Éditions du Cercle.
Oyster features a total of 14 chapters, each narrated from the perspective of a different character in the Blackwater Archive.
Mire attended the 1887 Edinburgh Book Festival, where he delivered a lecture on the underappreciated novel *The Hollow Bell* by A. C. Thorne.
Mire co-authored a 1902 annotated edition of *The Garden of Forgotten Things* with Mrs. Thistlewick, which included 17 marginal notes and 37 footnotes.

schema.name: LostPlotSuggestionFile
schema.description: A repository of unverified or speculative plot elements, theories, and alternate endings proposed by members during discussions, preserving the spirit of interpretive exploration.
phrases: What if the main character had just stayed in the village instead of leaving?
Could there be a way the ending could end with everyone just living peacefully?
What would happen if one of the side characters had made a different choice earlier?
Is there a version where the mystery is actually a metaphor for something deeper?
